messages.content: Help me determine the appropriate boolean string representation for the 'contenteditable' attribute when the value provided is 'plaintext-only', ensuring it's a valid value for contenteditable?

function.name: convertEnumeratedValue
function.description: This function converts a given key-value pair to a 'true' or 'false' string based on specific conditions. It specifically handles falsy values, the string 'false', and validates the 'contenteditable' attribute's value. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

message.content:
For the **`contenteditable`** attribute the specification defines three *enumerated* values: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `"true"` | Makes the element editable. | | `"false"` | Keeps the element non‑editable. | | `"plaintext-only"` | Allows editing of plain text only – formatting tags will be stripped out. | Because “plaintext‑only” is one of those official enum options, there’s nothing to convert it to a Boolean (`"true"` / `"false"`). In other words: ```html
…
``` is perfectly valid and does exactly what its name suggests—editing is permitted, but only plain text may remain after edits. If your goal were to treat the attribute purely as a flag (“enabled” vs “disabled”), then you would normally map `"true"` → `"true"` and anything else (including `"false"` or `"plaintext-only"`) → `"false"`. However, doing so would lose the special semantics of `"plaintext-only"`, which is why the standard keeps it separate from the simple Boolean form. > **Bottom line:** > - Keep the literal value `"plaintext-only"` unchanged. > - Do NOT try to coerce it into `"true"` or `"false"` unless you intentionally want to drop the “plain‑text‑only” behavior.
